extracted.intended_audience: Recipients and prospective accepters of NEH Public Scholar awards (2017–2018)
extracted.subtask_description: Official terms, conditions, and instructions for accepting and administering a 2017–2018 NEH Public Scholar award, including time commitments, allowable activities, reporting, payment procedures, acknowledgments, and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Scholar term periods may range between a minimum of six months and a maximum of twelve months. Terms must be continuous; no breaks from work on the project are allowable for the duration of the award. However, you may hold your award full-time, part-time, or a combination of the two. (Part-time is defined as a commitment to the project of anywhere between half-time and full-time.) Recipients must work at least half-time on their projects for the entire period of their term, and recipients who work full-time on their projects must forgo other major activities, including teaching. In any case--whether full-time, part-time, or a combination of the two--no term may exceed twelve months. You must complete your project work plan within twelve months of your chosen start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have questions, please contact the Public Scholar Program staff before accepting your award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in Project Scope or Plan of Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Your project must be consistent with the scope of the proposal that NEH has approved for funding. The scope of a project encompasses the purpose for which the award is undertaken, the subject matter, the treatment of the subject matter, the plans for travel, and the products that are expected to result. You must also adhere to the plan of work you specify when you accept the award, including the period of the award and your time commitment to the project (full- or part-time) during that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must describe and justify in writing any proposed changes in your project's scope or your plan of work so that NEH can determine whether they fall within the intent of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work Leading toward Degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: You may audit courses and seminars pertinent to your Public Scholar project, but you may not enroll in a degree program or engage in work you intend to apply toward a degree either now or later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation or Termination
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH may terminate your Public Scholar award if, for any reason, you resign or discontinue the proposed program before the end of the award period or fail to observe the award’s terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you resign before the end of your term, you must return any funds received over and above those to which you are entitled. If you are unable to meet the terms during the award period, inform NEH immediately; because stipend payments are made in advance, you may be required to return a portion of the stipend. NEH will inform you of the amount, the basis for the calculation, and the repayment date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Report
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit a final performance report on the activities you have accomplished with your NEH award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the final performance report electronically via eGMS within 90 days after the conclusion of your term. When accessing eGMS for the first time use the username from the Official Notice of Action and reset your password; a user guide is available on the eGMS site. A final financial report is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on the Use of Funds for Lobbying Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not use appropriated funds to influence the Executive or Legislative Branches of the federal government in connection with the award, per the Byrd Anti-Lobbying Amendment (31 U.S.C. 1352) and 18 U.S.C. 1913.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unallowable charges include certain electioneering activities, financial support for political parties, attempts to influence federal or state legislation directly or through grassroots lobbying, and some legislative liaison activities. The text of 18 U.S.C. 1913 is included; violations may constitute violations of 31 U.S.C. 1352(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will take appropriate action against individuals or organizations upon a determination that misconduct has occurred in proposing, performing, or reviewing research or reporting results from research activities funded by NEH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions are taken in accordance with the NEH Research Misconduct Policy (refer to the policy for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and Public Appearances Resulting from Your NEH Award
rubrics_metrics.description: You may copyright any material produced as a result of award activities, and you may make the results of your work available to the public without restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By accepting the award you agree, if requested, to provide excerpts for Humanities magazine, to participate in NEH-sponsored public events on mutually acceptable terms, and to provide advance notice of other public appearances so NEH may publicize them. NEH has a guide for grantees on publicizing projects and media tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Acknowledgment of NEH Support
rubrics_metrics.description: All products resulting from the NEH award (books, articles, films, videos, radio programs, databases, reports, Web resources, exhibits, etc.) must contain an acknowledgment of NEH support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The acknowledgment must include the statement: 'Any views, findings, conclusions, or recommendations expressed in this (publication) (program) (website) do not necessarily reflect those of the National Endowment for the Humanities.' Where possible, mention NEH support in publicity, media appearances, social media postings, book-signings, press conferences, or other public events. The NEH logo is available online. NEH has additional specific requirements for acknowledgements in films, videos, audio, and radio—consult NEH staff for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Humanities Council Notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Your state humanities council must be notified of your award and, wherever possible, given advance notice of any related public events occurring in the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of state humanities councils is provided on the NEH website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of Products to NEH and Use of Your Application
rubrics_metrics.description: You should forward one copy of all award products to the NEH as soon as they are available, no matter how long after grant completion the publication may appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the award period and in accordance with disclosure laws, NEH may make available to the public the narrative and bibliography you submitted with your application, including publishing samples of successful applications on NEH's website or in workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical Insurance and Other Fringe Benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH provides neither medical insurance nor any other fringe benefits for awardees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended that you continue any benefit programs in which you are participating. Unemployment compensation and Social Security insurance are not covered because NEH Public Scholars are not employees of the U.S. Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income Tax
rubrics_metrics.description: The tax laws determine the extent to which a particular award is taxable; NEH does not withhold taxes from stipends and does not send W-2 or 1099 forms to recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with tax laws to determine tax liability and whether you may deduct any expenses. NEH cannot provide tax advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities Outside the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to undertaking activities outside the United States, recipients shall secure the necessary passports, visas, or other required documents for entry into foreign countries and obtain appropriate licenses, permits, or approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify NEH if a permit is denied or revoked after an award is issued, or if unforeseen circumstances (natural disaster, political turmoil) threaten or prevent project activities. NEH does not assume responsibility for compliance with foreign laws. Consult State Department travel advisories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you have submitted your completed and signed acceptance form, NEH will send you an award letter that includes the payment schedule and instructions explaining how to submit your banking information to the NEH Accounting Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit banking information until you receive your award letter. You will be required to submit the ACH Vendor/Miscellaneous Payment Enrollment Form (Standard Form 3881) with a handwritten signature by the authorized certifying official at your institution’s bank or your bank. Return the signed form to the NEH Accounting Office by email or fax. Your NEH-assigned award number (beginning with FZ) must be on the ACH form for payment to be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance Form Usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The acceptance form is used to accept an NEH Public Scholar award and to indicate the exact term dates of your award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain a copy of the completed form for your records and notify the Public Scholar Program whenever you make modifications to arrangements agreed to by NEH. The acceptance form must include specified information (application number, name, SSN, contact info, term dates, payment preferences, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Number Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Include your application number (a two-letter prefix FZ plus six digits) on the acceptance form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application number can be found on your offer letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal and Contact Information Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The acceptance form must include your name, Social Security Number, mailing address, home and office phone numbers, and email address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term Dates (start/end rules and continuity)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may start your Public Scholar term any month during the thirteen-month window; your term must begin on the first day of your chosen month and end on the last day of your chosen final month. Remember that you must complete your Public Scholar term within twelve months of the initial month you choose. Your Public Scholar term must be continuous; no breaks from work on the project are allowable for the duration of your award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards may be held full-time, part-time, or a combination. Part-time is defined as a commitment anywhere between half-time and full-time. You must work at least half-time for the entire grant period. The term dates you provide on the acceptance form may differ from the dates you originally requested in your application, but you may not increase the length of your term beyond your original request (you may decrease it). Be certain of the term dates you enter on the acceptance form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend Calculation and Worksheet
rubrics_metrics.description: The final amount of the stipend is based on the number of full-time equivalent months of your term. For each month of your term, NEH provides $4,200.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: full-time 12 months = $50,400; half-time 12 months = $25,200; three-quarter-time 12 months = $37,800. The acceptance form includes a worksheet for plotting your award term; list periods chronologically and account for the entire term. NEH will use this to establish a payment schedule, so accuracy is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent Funding and Multiple Awards Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: You may concurrently hold non-NEH funding support for the same project during your NEH Public Scholar term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may not accept or hold more than one NEH individual award (Public Scholar, Fellowship, Award for Faculty, or Summer Stipend) in a given fiscal year (October–September). Nor may you work on a project supported by an NEH institutional award while holding an NEH individual award on a full-time basis. Contact staff if you have questions about multiple awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: How Stipend Is Paid (payment method and scheduling)
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH pays award stipends in installments and prorates them according to the term length. Typically, the first payment is made at the beginning of the term period and subsequent payments are made every third month through the award term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All payments are made electronically by the U.S. Treasury via ACH. You may have payments deposited into your bank account or your employing institution’s bank account—choose only one. If deposited to an institution, some institutions may continue paying fringe benefits and may return unspent award funds to you at the end of the award period. Payments cannot be sent to foreign addresses or deposited in non-U.S. banks. NOTE: The acceptance form does NOT request banking information; you will receive separate instructions with the award letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early First Payment
rubrics_metrics.description: You may receive your first payment 30 days before your term begins if you anticipate major travel expenses early in your term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, no payment can be made before September 1, 2017.

rubrics_metrics.name: Larger First Payment for High Initial Expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have particularly high initial expenses, you may receive a larger first payment to cover them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and Certification Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: You must accept or decline the offer of a 2017–2018 NEH Public Scholar award no later than September 18, 2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To accept the award, complete, sign, and return the acceptance form to the NEH Public Scholar Program by either scanning and emailing it to the specified email or faxing it to (202) 606-8204 by this deadline.
